# `delivery` commands

## `delivery approve`

A person's go for ready messages waiting for one (an agent's release): by number, or all_waiting. A message leaves only with a go, and only through a sending connection. Needs delivery.send. Example: {"messages": ["M-1001"]}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | customer |
| Additional resources | ledger.read: member, customer-work: member |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/delivery.approve` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow delivery approve --all-waiting --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Checked them" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "delivery approve", "input": {"all_waiting": true}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `messages` | `--messages` | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | Ready messages waiting for a go, by number or id. |
| `all_waiting` | `--all-waiting` | boolean | no | no | false | Every message waiting for a go (100 per call; it says when more wait). |
| `batch` | `--batch` | string \| null | no | yes | null | A batch's messages waiting for a go, only those still as the batch drafted them (100 per call). |

## `delivery batch`

Draft many messages in one act: queued (to-be-emailed documents), unsent with a kind (filters date_from, date_to, customer_type, customer), kind statement with period and balance_over (one per customer with a balance), or kind notice with ready. Always run it with dry_run first and show the person who gets what and who is skipped and why; then run it with the dry run's fingerprint (a changed set is refused). It drafts 10 per call and returns next: call again with it until done. reversal_batch_id identifies the shared reversal batch; next_commands includes its batch reverse preview. Only unchanged, unreleased drafts with no exported files can be reversed as a whole. send releases them too; combine puts a customer's documents in one message. To repeat it every month or day, use delivery-schedule create. Example: {"kind": "statement", "period": "2026-09", "balance_over": "0", "method": "email"}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | customer |
| Additional resources | ledger.read: member, customer-work: member |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/delivery.batch` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow delivery batch --kind statement --period 2026-11 --balance-over 0 --method email --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --dry-run --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:


## `delivery batch-cancel`

Cancel a batch as one unit, with --reason: every message it drafted that was never released or exported is cancelled; the ones that block (released, exported, sent) are named and stay.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | customer |
| Additional resources | ledger.read: member, customer-work: member |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/delivery.batch-cancel` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow delivery batch-cancel B-1001 --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Wrong month" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:


## `delivery cancel`

Set an unsent message aside, with --reason. Final; draft again for a new one.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |

## `delivery draft`

Draft one email to a customer with the document attached as a PDF, frozen now (file name, size and SHA-256 recorded): an invoice, sales-receipt or estimate (`document`), a statement (`customer`, `date_from`, `date_to`) or a ready overdue notice (`document`). To and Cc come from the customer, Bcc from the company's copy-to; subject and body from the kind's default template unless given. A second draft of the same document returns the first while it is in the outbox; one already sent needs `again`. Nothing is sent. Example: {"kind": "invoice", "document": "1007"}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | customer |
| Additional resources | ledger.read: member, customer-work: member |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/delivery.draft` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow delivery draft invoice DEMO-SALE-INV-ACTIVE --to '["ap@example.com"]' --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Customer asked for a copy" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "delivery draft", "input": {"kind": "invoice", "document": "DEMO-SALE-INV-ACTIVE", "to": ["ap@example.com"]}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

| `document` | `DOCUMENT` | string \| null | no | yes | null | The invoice, sales receipt or estimate (number or id), or the overdue notice (id). |
| `customer` | `--customer` | string \| null | no | yes | null | A statement: the customer or job, by name or id. |
| `date_from` | `--date-from` | string \| null | no | yes | null | A statement: first day of the period. |
| `date_to` | `--date-to` | string \| null | no | yes | null | A statement: last day of the period. |
| `template` | `--template` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Template by name or id; default the kind's default. |
| `to` | `--to` | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | To; default the customer's email (a job without one uses its parent's). |
| `cc` | `--cc` | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | Cc; default the customer's cc email. |

| `body` | `--body` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Body, instead of the template's. |

## `delivery export`

Export messages as RFC 5322 .eml files (X-Unsent: 1) with their frozen PDFs, to open and send in a mail program: one message gives a .eml, several a .zip. Sends nothing; a stale message is held instead of exported.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | customer |
| Additional resources | ledger.read: member, customer-work: member |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/delivery.export` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow delivery export --messages '["M-1001"]' --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "To send by hand" --json`

### MCP

## `delivery retry`

Put a failed message, or one held because an attempt ended without an answer, back in the outbox. Check the sent mail first: if it went, mark it sent instead. A person's retry is their go; an agent's waits.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Scope | company |

## `delivery run`

One dispatch pass now: claim due messages with a go, send each through the sending connection, record what it said (sent, try again later, failed, or held when the answer is unknown). With no connection it claims nothing. The host does this on its own about once a minute.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | customer |
| Additional resources | ledger.read: member, customer-work: member |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/delivery.run` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow delivery run --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Send what is due" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "delivery run", "input": {}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `limit` | `--limit` | integer | no | no | 10 | Most messages to claim in this pass.; minimum 1; maximum 50 |

### Command and context options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Print one JSON object. |

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.

## `delivery send`

Release drafts to the outbox (ready). A person's release is also their go; an agent's waits for one. No sending connection exists yet, so a ready message waits there; export it to send it yourself. A message whose document changed or was voided is held instead.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

|---|---|
| Scope | company |

| Capability | customer |
| Additional resources | ledger.read: member, customer-work: member |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/delivery.send` |
| External binary body | none |

## `delivery unflag`

Mark a document never to email: an explicit opt-out, which wins over the company's auto-flag date. clear removes the flag instead (back to neutral).

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | customer |
| Additional resources | ledger.read: member, customer-work: member |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/delivery.unflag` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow delivery unflag invoice DEMO-SALE-INV-ACTIVE --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "They want it by post" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "delivery unflag", "input": {"kind": "invoice", "document": "DEMO-SALE-INV-ACTIVE"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |

| `kind` | `KIND` | literal["invoice", "sales-receipt", "estimate"] | yes | no | — | invoice, sales-receipt or estimate. |
| `document` | `DOCUMENT` | string | yes | no | — | The document, by number or id.; minimum length 1; maximum length 1004 |
| `clear` | `--clear` | boolean | no | no | false | Remove the flag instead: back to neutral, where the auto-flag date decides. Without it, an explicit opt-out (never email this). |

## `delivery update`

Edit a draft or held message: To, Cc, Bcc, subject or body. The attachments stay as drafted unless `refresh`, which attaches the document as it is now and releases a changed-document hold.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.
